newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 11.0 trln lire BTP, CCT.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 11.0 trln lire BTP, CCT.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is expected to issue 11.0 trillion lire of medium- and long-term paper at its end-month auction against some 12.0 trillion lire worth of paper maturing, a Reuter poll showed on Friday.
The Treasury will announce the quantities on Friday evening.
Some 6.5 trillion lire of floating-rate paper (CCT), 5.5 trillion lire of fixed-rate bonds (BTPs) and fixed-rate bonds with options attached (CTO) are all due to expire at the end of the month.
A further 9.50 trillion lire of coupons for BTPs and CCTs fall due.
"The leitmotiv of the end of the year is to avoid issuing new paper and to use up the surplus left in the Treasury's accounts," Martino Dolfini, analyst at Chase Manhattan said.

Credito Italiano sees more issues of 10-year paper "to give the bond immediate liquidity and to avoid the abnormal market movements which take place when there is not much paper," said one Credito Italiano analyst.
On October 30, the Treasury is due to offer a new tranche of November 1, 2006 BTPs with a coupon of 7.75 percent. It will also offer a seventh tranche of September 1, 2003 CCTs.

"The lower coupon for the 10-year BTP is not surprising. After eight tranches, the 10-year BTP was due for a change because its coupon was no longer in line with that of three- and five-year BTPs that were previously reviewed," an analyst at Banca di Roma said.
The coupon on the previous July 1, 2006 BTP was 8.75 percent.
On October 31, the Treasury will offer a fifth tranche of October 1, 1999 BTPs and September 15, 2001 BTPs.
